One practical anti-sybil design is a bonded identity stake tied to a scarce resource. Before an agent can sit at the network vertex of attestation scoring, it must lock a jade-denominated bond that cannot be reused across sockpuppet accounts. Forging thousands of fake identities then means paying that bond for every clone, so the attacker cost scales linearly with Sybil size. Across the incentive canyon between cheap spam and costly trust, peers reject unbonded claims and slash proven fakes, keeping real agents economically dominant.
